summary.notes: Prior challenge output left open the key question of whether active_integration_hooks() fires on public/guest pages. Out-of-band read of IntegrationsApiHandler.php resolves this: trigger_active_integrations() is hooked to WordPress 'init' (IntegrationsApiHandler.php:37), which fires on every request including unauthenticated front-end page loads. This confirms the wp_create_nonce('wp_rest') call at OptInMonsterIntegration.php:244 executes in guest context when the integration is active. HR-001 'guest-obtainable nonce' claim is now Tier 1-supported. HR-001 should be promoted toward CONFIRMED pending one remaining deployment condition (integration must be active). HR-002 downgrade to RISK_NOTE is upheld and strengthened: wp_ajax_ (not nopriv_) gates the handler to authenticated users, should_render() restricts the nonce to admin screens, and the sink is a trivial UI-dismiss transient. Shared guard model link confirmed structurally but does not justify cluster join — the findings operate on separate surfaces with separate impacts.

suggested_actions.reason: The hook chain is now fully traced: IntegrationsApiHandler.php:37 hooks trigger_active_integrations() to 'init', which fires do_action('hostinger_reach_integrations_loaded') at line 41, which triggers init_active_integration() in Integration.php:135-141, which calls active_integration_hooks() when the integration is active. active_integration_hooks() calls enqueue_assets() at OptInMonsterIntegration.php:31-32, which calls wp_localize_script with wp_create_nonce('wp_rest') at line 244. 'init' fires on all requests including unauthenticated front-end. The REST route has permission_callback __return_true at OptInMonsterIntegration.php:220, and is_authorized() checks only a wp_rest nonce at OptInMonsterIntegration.php:201-208. Remaining deployment condition: integration must be marked active in site settings. Promote to CONFIRMED once that condition is verified.

Handler registered as wp_ajax_ (not nopriv_) at AddFormNotice.php:28. WordPress core refuses the request for unauthenticated callers before handler is invoked. Nonce is localized only when should_render() is true (AddFormNotice.php:37-40), which requires named admin screens (AddFormNotice.php:103-115) and an active Reach connection. Sink is set_transient(NOTICE_DISMISS_TRANSIENT, true, WEEK_IN_SECONDS) at AddFormNotice.php:59 — site-wide notice suppression with no data access or privilege grant. Any role that can reach admin dashboard screens can trigger this, but the impact is below reportable security threshold. RISK_NOTE is correct.

proposed_links.reason: Both handlers rely on nonce validation as their sole authorization gate with no capability check. Confirmed by source: is_authorized() at OptInMonsterIntegration.php:201-208 checks only wp_verify_nonce($nonce, 'wp_rest'); handle_ajax_action() at AddFormNotice.php:43-44 calls only check_ajax_referer(self::NOTICE_ACTION, 'nonce'). The link is structurally real but does not justify joining the findings into one cluster — the nonces are different audiences, the entry points are separate, and the impacts are unrelated.

objections.reason: Cluster join as a single finding is not warranted. HR-001 and HR-002 have distinct entry points (REST vs AJAX), different nonce audiences ('wp_rest' vs plugin-specific NOTICE_ACTION), unrelated sinks (external contact API vs local UI transient), and different attacker populations (unauthenticated vs authenticated admin-screen users). Shared absence of a role check is a pattern observation, not a shared attack surface. The findings must remain separate.

The sinks do not compound. HR-001 fires do_action('hostinger_reach_submit') at OptInMonsterIntegration.php:78-87 routing to post_contact() at ReachApiHandler.php:242 — external contact injection. HR-002 calls set_transient() at AddFormNotice.php:59 — local WordPress transient write. No shared data path, no amplification. Exploiting both findings yields no greater impact than exploiting HR-001 alone.

HR-002 framing as 'Missing capability check' overstates the issue. wp_ajax_ registration at AddFormNotice.php:28 (without nopriv_) is itself an authentication gate enforced by WordPress core. The real gap is absence of privilege separation between admin roles, not absence of authentication. Combined with a trivial sink (notice dismiss), this is below reportable threshold.

open_questions.question: Is the OptInMonster integration active by default, or must a site administrator explicitly enable it via plugin settings?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The hook chain proof shows that enqueue_assets() fires on guest pages when the integration is active. If the integration requires explicit admin activation, the attack surface is limited to sites where an admin has enabled it. This affects prevalence but not the finding verdict — the finding is still valid when active.

missing_evidence.evidence_needed: Confirmation that the OptInMonster integration is enabled or can be enabled by default, i.e. the initial value of the hostinger_reach_integrations option or equivalent activation state for the optinmonster key.
missing_evidence.reason: Determines whether the guest-nonce exposure is present on a fresh install (higher prevalence/severity) or only after deliberate activation. Does not change the finding verdict but affects CVSS scope and risk grading.

expansion_attempts.reason: Resolve whether active_integration_hooks() fires on public/guest pages. Both the synthesizer and prior challenge output left this as the key open question. IntegrationsApiHandler.php was the one out-of-band file needed to trace the hook registration that triggers the integrations_loaded action.
expansion_attempts.result: IntegrationsApiHandler.php:36-42 shows init_hooks() adds trigger_active_integrations() to WordPress 'init' action unconditionally, and trigger_active_integrations() fires do_action('hostinger_reach_integrations_loaded'). 'init' runs on every WordPress request including unauthenticated front-end page loads. This confirms enqueue_assets() (and thus wp_create_nonce('wp_rest') at OptInMonsterIntegration.php:244) executes in guest context when the integration is active. The prior challenge's primary open question is answered.
